ai.description: This small frog reaches 20–25 mm. It is brown with a distinct dark lateral stripe and a pale vertebral line. It features a prominent papilla on the tongue and lacks vomerine teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Liurana medogensis* is best distinguished from similar Indian species by the presence of a distinct, fleshy papilla on the dorsal surface of its tongue.
ai.habitat: *Liurana medogensis* inhabits high-altitude, mossy evergreen forests and rocky stream banks in the Himalayas, typically at elevations between 2,500 and 3,300 meters.
ai.behavior: *Liurana medogensis* is primarily nocturnal, often found active on moss-covered rocks or near stream banks within its high-altitude forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Liurana medogensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in terrestrial or semi-aquatic habitats. Its larvae undergo direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Liurana medogensis* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically within Arunachal Pradesh, India, at high elevations ranging from 2,300 to 3,400 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Medog Papilla-tongued Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard near small, rocky streams within its humid forest habitat.
